subject: Advance payment term request — 2/3yr prepay structure and approval
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Kapoor <sana.kapoor@uptick.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: advance-payment options for 2–3 year commitment

Hi Sana —

Great speaking earlier. As discussed, I attached an initial quote and two prepay structures for Uptick's 3-year plan. High level:

- Option A (3-yr full prepay): 25% list discount plus volume tiering; payment due at contract signing; priority capacity reservation.
- Option B (2-yr annual prepay ramp): 18% year-1 prepay, 12% year-2; payments at each year start; flexible scale-up in year 2 with a true-up.

I flagged the areas where we can be flexible: upfront discount depth, annual ramp tranches, and reserved burst capacity. If Procurement needs specific invoicing terms (PO/Net30/Net45) or KYC for financial sign-off, let me know and I’ll route.

Attachments: Uptick-Initial-Quote.pdf

Next steps: can you confirm which structure you prefer and the expected committed QPS / token volumes so I can run a firm pricing calc and prepare a prepay addendum?

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

2) For Option B (the ramp), can you confirm if unused tokens roll forward or if there's forfeiture? We prefer true-up/roll-forward if possible.
3) We may need a PO and an addendum that lists the committed QPS/units per year for audit — can Redwood provide the addendum template?

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Uptick prepay questions — approval needed for modified structure

Team — forwarding Uptick's procurement questions. They like a hybrid: a 3-year commitment but want annual prepay with roll-forward/true-up and 60-day invoice terms. Pricing ask: can we offer a 30% effective discount if Uptick agrees to a 3-year commitment with an annual prepay schedule and guaranteed min ARR of $1.2M in year 1 scaling to $1.8M in year 3?

Why urgency: they are targeting a procurement window that closes 7/28; loss of timing risks the expansion.

Requested: approval to offer a 30% effective discount under the following conditions: (a) signed prepay addendum with committed annual minimums and true-up; (b) Redwood reserves the right to withhold burst priority if actual usage > +50% of committed capacity without additional fees; (c) payment terms: Net30 after invoice but invoice can be issued at year start for annual prepay.

Attachments: RDW-Prepay-Addendum-draft.docx

Thanks —
Dylan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Uptick prepay questions — approval needed for modified structure

Dylan — thanks for the summary. High-level thoughts: a 30% effective discount is in range but needs finance and legal guardrails. Karthik — please confirm margin impact and whether we need a CFO sign-off threshold for >25% discount on multi-year prepay. Laura — please check the addendum for roll-forward language and whether we can carve priority capacity exceptions.

If finance signs off, I'm fine approving conditioned on pipeline sign-off and an executive sponsor acknowledgement (SaaS BB metrics, committed ARR, and churn protections). We should also ask for an initial non-refundable deposit (10% of year-1 committed ARR) to align incentives if they insist on extended invoice terms.

-Marissa
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Uptick prepay questions — approval needed for modified structure

Team — ran the numbers. A 30% effective discount on the proposed commit path has acceptable unit economics if we require either (A) an initial 10% non-refundable deposit applied to year-1 prepay, or (B) Net30 payment after invoice but with a financial guarantee (PO + parent company guarantee). Without one of those, the cash-on-hand risk increases and we’d push effective margin below threshold.

Also recommend: include a usage true-up clause (roll-forward up to 20% into next year; beyond that, usage billed at list) and a cap on reserved burst to 50% of committed QPS unless they buy burst credit.

I'll sign off on the 30% if Marissa & Laura agree to the deposit/guarantee and the addendum uses strict true-up language.

-Karthik
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Uptick prepay questions — approval needed for modified structure

Dylan / team — I reviewed the addendum draft. Edits I require before external send:

- Explicit roll-forward cap: "Unused prepay credits may be rolled forward to the following 12-month term up to 20% of the prior term's committed units."
- True-up timing and rate: "True-ups will be calculated within 30 days of term end and billed at standard list rates for overages."
- Invoicing: add a clause allowing invoicing at the start of each prepay term, with payment due Net30; if they request Net60 or 60-day lag, we need a signed deposit or parent guaranty.
- Burst priority: define "priority" as reserved compute capacity identified in Exhibit B; prioritization does not guarantee additional capacity beyond reserved burst unless purchased.

If those edits are ok with Finance, I can prepare a redline and we can send to Uptick with the 30% effective discount conditional on the deposit/guarantee.

-Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi Sana / Vikram — thanks for the patience while we aligned internally. Good news: we can offer the hybrid 3-year commitment with annual prepay/true-up and an effective 30% discount under the following conditions (summarized):

1) Commitments: minimum committed ARR of $1.2M year-1 scaling to $1.8M year-3 (as discussed).
2) Payment: Redwood will invoice at the start of each prepay term; standard payment due Net30. If Uptick requires extended payment terms (Net45/Net60), a 10% non-refundable deposit of year-1 ARR is required or a parent company guarantee must be provided.
3) Roll-forward: unused prepay credits may roll forward up to 20% into next term; overages billed at list rates and subject to true-up within 30 days of term end.
4) Priority capacity: reserved capacity defined in Exhibit B; burst priority is limited and additional burst capacity must be purchased if usage exceeds +50% of committed capacity.
5) Legal & Addendum: we’ll send a redlined prepay addendum documenting the above. Signature required to lock the pricing and discount.

Attached: RDW-Prepay-Addendum-draft.docx (redline forthcoming). Can you confirm whether Procurement can accept Net30 with the deposit? If not, please indicate the PO/guaranty route and timeline — Procurement stated their window closes 7/28, so a response by end of week would keep this slot.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
